Rarity.rationale: Vajra.cs:15. Common in the transcribed grab bag (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py pool -> bag=Common), so it is obtainable from any Common pull.

AfterRoomEntered.rationale: Vajra.cs:21-28 applies StrengthPower(1) from AfterRoomEntered when `room is CombatRoom`; the port applies it from on_combat_start. The EFFECT is identical (see guard N1 for the executed value) but the PHASE differs, and it differs by more than a hook slot: for a CombatRoom the game fires Hook.AfterRoomEntered at CombatRoom.cs:228, immediately after SetUpCombat and BEFORE CombatManager.AfterCombatRoomLoaded -> StartCombatInternal (CombatManager.cs:380-403), which is where AfterCreatureAdded, every enemy's first Monster.RollMove and only then Hook.BeforeCombatStart happen. So in the game the +1 Strength is on the player before the first intents are rolled; in the sim it lands at turn_structure step 3, after the monsters have already telegraphed (turn_structure step 2 / guard G9). Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because the window genuinely exists and an effect placed in it would expose the difference -- the same treatment audit/records/relic/brilliant_scarf.json gives its BeforeSideTurnStart entry. See guard G1 for why it is not filed as a live gap. Rule 7: CombatRoom.cs, CombatManager.cs and audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): nothing observes the player's Strength in the window between C#'s AfterRoomEntered and the sim's on_combat_start, so the phase difference has no observable today
guards.issue: MECHANISM: as above -- one full combat-setup phase separates the two positions, and it contains AfterCreatureAdded plus every enemy's opening RollMove. TWO readers could expose it and neither exists in ported content. (a) A monster whose move selection reads the PLAYER's Strength: executed census (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py vajra) finds only three ported monster modules that mention strength at all -- sts2_rl/monsters/fuzzy_wurm_crawler.py, sts2_rl/monsters/overgrowth/fuzzy_wurm_crawler.py and sts2_rl/monsters/glory/aeonglass.py -- and all three read or grant their OWN Strength (sts2_rl/monsters/fuzzy_wurm_crawler.py:36-40 and sts2_rl/monsters/overgrowth/fuzzy_wurm_crawler.py:37-41 each build a self-buff intent, aeonglass.py:37, 85-87 tracks its own escalation). (b) A ported on_combat_start listener that reads player Strength: the six other relics that touch Strength at combat start all WRITE it and none reads it (ember_tea.py:28-33, philosophers_stone.py:28-32, red_skull.py:42-43 reads HP not Strength, sling_of_courage.py:20-28, sword_of_jade.py:22-29). The sim's registration-order dependence is real and executed: with a spy relic registered before Vajra the spy reads Strength 0 from on_combat_start, registered after it reads 1, where C# reads 1 either way because Vajra's hook belongs to an earlier phase. DORMANT; what would make it live is either porting a monster whose intent selection reads the player's Strength, or porting any BeforeCombatStart listener that does (Red Skull's C# sibling shape -- a combat-start reader -- is the obvious candidate). Filed as a gap and not a waiver because 'no ported content triggers this' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Rule 7: the six sts2_rl/relics/*.py and three sts2_rl/monsters/*.py files named here are NOT hashed by this record. [CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-26 by the relic fix pass: the path was written as a bare basename plus line range (`fuzzy_wurm_crawler` `.py:36-40`), which audit/tools/backfill_sources.py cannot resolve -- the repo has two files of that name, and the record's own census names both -- so the citation was discarded and neither file pinned. Both are now spelled out, with the overgrowth copy's line range corrected to 37-41 (its `current_intent` body sits one line lower because of the extra package level in `from ...powers import StrengthPower`).]

guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in Vajra.cs, so 1 is the pinned non-ascension value. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py vajra): turn 1 opens with Strength = 1, matching C#.

guards.what: N2: C# passes applier = target = base.Owner.Creature and cardSource = null (Vajra.cs:26); the sim passes applier=self.player, target=self.player, no card (vajra.py:17)
guards.rationale: Both sides name the player as applier and as target, and neither passes a card source. Checked deliberately because relic/unsettling_lamp's doubling requires `applier is self.player AND target is not self.player` (audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json guard G3): a self-targeted Strength buff can never satisfy the second half, so no Lamp interaction exists on either side. The `new ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext()` argument is the multiplayer choice plumbing -- noted in the mapping, not a divergence (shared contract, Scope).

guards.what: N3: `room is CombatRoom` is the only guard, and it decides HOW OFTEN the relic fires
guards.rationale: C# fires once per CombatRoom entry; the sim fires once per CombatState construction, and the sim builds exactly one CombatState per combat room (run.py:1123 create_combat is called per resolved encounter). A map point with more than one room enters CombatRoom again in the game and gets a second application, which the sim reproduces by building a second CombatState. Recorded because the sim ALSO has a real after_room_entered hook (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:194-195, dispatched at run.py:983) that this port could have used -- and deliberately should not, because at that moment no CombatState exists to hold the power. That is what makes the AfterRoomEntered entry a divergence rather than a missing hook. Rule 7: sts2_rl/relics/base.py and run.py are NOT hashed here.

RelicModel.Flash() / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow and hover text. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
